title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). X is a stratified space whose strata X_i^* are indexed by a poset I. Here i ≤ k means that X_i^* lies in the closure X_k, and X_k is the disjoint union of the X_i^* for i ≤ k. A 'bande' J ⊂ I is a convex subset: j0 ≤ i ≤ j with j0, j ∈ J implies i ∈ J. Then X_J^* = ∪_{i∈J} X_i^* is locally closed. Ideals give closed unions of strata and coideals give open ones. Each stratum has a (pro-)tubular neighbourhood V_i, with V_ij = V_i ∩ V_j; this is the 'déploiement' data.

Formula (62) defines the pro-tubular neighbourhood of X_J^* in X as V_J = ∪_{i∈J} V_i = colim over i, j ∈ J of the diagram (V_i, V_ij). So the neighbourhood of a convex union of strata is glued from the neighbourhoods of the individual strata.

Formula (63) defines, for two bandes J and L, V_J^L := V_J ∩ X_L^*. This is the trace of the neighbourhood of X_J^* on the union of strata X_L^*. For J = {i}, L = {l} with i < l it is the part of the tube around X_i^* lying in the stratum X_l^*: a deleted-neighbourhood or 'link' object, homotopically Quinn's homotopy link. In general it is a link between two convex unions of strata.

Formula (64): V_J^J = X_J^*, so the strata themselves are the diagonal case.

The margin records the gluing ('recollement') data between X_J^* and X_L^*: V_J^L ↪ X_L^* ↪ V_L and V_J^L ↪ V_J.

Formula (65): define L_0 = {l ∈ L : l ≥ some j ∈ J} and J_0 = {j ∈ J : j ≤ some l ∈ L}. Then V_J^L = V_J^{L_0} = V_{J_0}^L = V_{J_0}^{L_0}. Here J_0 is an ideal of J, L_0 is a coideal of L, and J_0 ≺ L_0.

Formula (66) introduces the 'domination' relation J ≺ L: every element of J lies below some element of L, and every element of L lies above some element of J. The next page proves a lemma: J ≺ L with J, L bandes is equivalent to the existence of a (unique, minimal) bande I' = {i : j ≤ i ≤ l for some j ∈ J, l ∈ L} in which J is an ideal and L a coideal. Geometrically, X_J^* is then closed and X_L^* open in X_{I'}^*. So V_J^L is the link of a closed union of strata inside an open union of strata, within one locally closed stratified piece.

Purpose: build the combinatorial-topological bookkeeping needed to describe a tame stratified space by its strata plus link and recollement data indexed by pairs of bandes. This is the 'déploiement' / reconstruction theorem announced in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: (65) silently needs V_i ∩ X_l^* = ∅ unless i ≤ l. This holds under the frontier condition and for small enough (germs of) tubular neighbourhoods, but is not stated on the page.

After (65) the text says every element of L_0 is 'majoré' by an element of J_0; this should be 'majore' (lies above), as in definition (66). The reduction itself is correct: if j ≤ l with j ∈ J and l ∈ L, then j ∈ J_0 and l ∈ L_0, so J_0 ≺ L_0.
Since the V's are pro-objects (germs), 'union' and 'intersection' should be read levelwise or as pro-objects; the page treats them as honest open sets.

ideas.what: Neighbourhood of a convex union of strata obtained as the colimit/union of the tubular neighbourhoods of the strata (62)
ideas.modern_name: gluing of tubular neighbourhoods / control data (Mather–Thom)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches tubular neighbourhoods and déploiement for tame stratified spaces, without these formulas

ideas.what: V_J^L = V_J ∩ X_L^* as a generalized link between two bandes, with recollement maps V_J^L → X_L^*, V_J^L → V_J
ideas.modern_name: homotopy links / links of strata; decollage or recollement data of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Lurie (HA A.6); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (links, unzipping); Woolf, Miller, Haine, Douteau, Waas
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme (reconstructing a stratified space from strata and links) appears in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Domination relation J ≺ L between convex subsets of a poset, characterized via a minimal ambient bande in which J is an ideal and L a coideal
ideas.modern_name: intervals/convex subposets; ideal–coideal (closed–open) decomposition; relates to chains in the subdivision sd(P)

missed.claim: Links are indexed not by chains of strata (as in Quinn, Lurie's exit paths, or Haine's sd(P)-diagrams) but by pairs of convex subsets J ≺ L, i.e. links of a closed union of strata in an open union inside a locally closed piece. This yields a recollement presentation of a stratified space indexed by such pairs. It is close to, but packaged differently from, the 'generalized homotopy links' of Douteau and Waas and the unzipping of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka.
missed.quote: V_J^L ≝ V_J ∩ X_L^* , où J, L sont deux bandes ... la relation de domination J ≺ L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a coarser, convex-subset-indexed system of links that might simplify descriptions of stratified homotopy types or constructible sheaves via closed/open recollement at the level of unions of strata. However, the page is mainly bookkeeping, and equivalent data are recoverable from chain-indexed holinks.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful foundational preliminaries for the déploiement programme announced in Esquisse. Indexing links by pairs of bandes under the domination relation is a mildly distinctive organization not found verbatim in the literature, but the mathematics is elementary and conceptually anticipated by Quinn, Lurie and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka.
transcription_corrections: The marginal note reads roughly 'prolongement de recollement entre X_J^* et X_L^* : V_J^L ↪ X_L^* ↪ V_L, V_J^L ↪ V_J' (the vertical arrow goes from V_J^L down to V_J). It is followed by heavily scribbled-out text.
In the passage after (65), 'tout élément de L_0 est majoré par un élément de J_0' should mathematically be 'majore'; the handwriting is ambiguous.
The top-right inserted example reads roughly: 'Ex: J ⊂ J' inclusion de bandes, K (idéal de J'), d'où X_J^* ⊂ X_{J'}^*, on prend V(X_J^*, X_{J'}^*) ∩ X_K^*'.
